title: Purpose Connectors: Con El Fin de, Con Miras A

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the purpose phrases *con miras a* and *con vistas a* from B2 Unit 12: *con el fin de* + infinitive, *con miras a* and *con vistas a* "with a view to" + infinitive or noun, and *de modo que* + subjunctive when the subject changes. After a disaster and a debt crisis, people and institutions act for a purpose, and these phrases say what for.

sections.title: What is it for?
rows: La ley creó una junta con el fin de controlar el presupuesto.
*con el fin de* + infinitive: in order to
Instalaron paneles solares con miras a tener electricidad durante los apagones.
*con miras a* + infinitive: with a view to
Se preparan con vistas a la próxima temporada de huracanes.
*con vistas a* + noun: with a view to
Repartieron agua de modo que todos los vecinos pudieran beber.
*de modo que* + subjunctive: so that (two subjects)

items.spanish: Muchas comunidades se organizaron con el fin de repartir agua y comida.
items.english: Many communities organised in order to hand out water and food.

items.spanish: Casa Pueblo instaló paneles solares con miras a tener electricidad durante los apagones.
items.english: Casa Pueblo installed solar panels with a view to having electricity during blackouts.

items.spanish: El gobierno publicó la lista con vistas a la reunión de la Junta.
items.english: The government published the list with the Board's meeting in mind.

items.spanish: Repartieron agua de modo que todos los vecinos pudieran beber.
items.english: They handed out water so that all the neighbours could drink.

sections.content: The preposition after *fin* is *de*, and after *miras* and *vistas* it is always *a*, never *para* or *en*. After *con el fin de* and *con miras a* use an infinitive when you name the action. Use *de modo que* + subjunctive when a different person does the next action: *de modo que todos pudieran beber*.
